title: Keep unwanted files out
summary: A .dockerignore file excludes matching files from the build context. This keeps temporary or private files out of a build.
introduction: A .dockerignore file excludes matching files from the build context. This keeps temporary or private files out of a build. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A .dockerignore file excludes matching files from the build context. This keeps temporary or private files out of a build.
These patterns exclude Git history, installed packages, a common environment file and log files.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add a pattern for a local scratch directory.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Ignoring a file in Git and ignoring it in a Docker build are separate settings.
For more detail later, use this [Docker further reading](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/).
